The schedule is unique, and it matches my earlier answer.

Ivo, Dev, Gus and Elif form a consecutive block at slots p to p+3, since Dev = Ivo+1, Gus = Dev+1 and Elif = Gus+1. "Exactly one person between Gus and Ivo" gives |G−I| = 2, which is already satisfied. Ann is before Dev and at least three slots from Ivo, so Ann is at or before p−3. Ben = Ann+1, Hana = Ann−1, and Finn = Ben+1 form a consecutive run of four (Hana, Ann, Ben, Finn) that sits entirely left of the Ivo block. Cara must be before Hana, which forces Cara onto the left side as well. That fills slots 1–5 and puts the Ivo block at 6–9.

Checking all 15 constraints against this arrangement, every one holds: Gus = Dev+1, Ann = Hana+1, Dev < Gus, |Ben−Cara| = 3, Ben < Gus, Dev = Ivo+1, |Ben−Elif| = 5, Finn = Ben+1, |Gus−Ivo| = 2, Ann < Dev, |Finn−Hana| = 3, Elif = Gus+1, |Ann−Ivo| = 3, Cara < Hana, and Ben = Ann+1.

SCHEDULE: {"1":"Cara","2":"Hana","3":"Ann","4":"Ben","5":"Finn","6":"Ivo","7":"Dev","8":"Gus","9":"Elif"}
CONFIDENCE: 98
